data.title: RepoGlance
data.description: RepoGlance puts your GitHub repositories on your Pixel home screen: open issues and pull requests, latest pushes, and how old each number is. Read-only, with no server.

layout.heading: Glance at the home screen. Know where your repos stand.
layout.lead: Your pinned repositories, latest push first. How many issues and pull requests are open, and how old that count is. One tap and the thread opens in the GitHub app. RepoGlance only reads; it never changes anything on GitHub.

$media.alt: A Pixel home screen with the RepoGlance Pinned repos widget listing three made-up repositories and the compact Repository widget below it, each row with the time of its data and its open issue and pull request counts

A Pixel home screen with the RepoGlance Pinned repos widget listing three made-up repositories and the compact Repository widget below it, each row with the time of its data and its open issue and pull request counts

layout.heading: On the home screen
layout.body: The Pinned repos widget lists what you pinned, most recent push first. The Repository widget shows a repository's open issue and pull request counts, with the latest items at the taller size. Both say how old their numbers are.

$media.alt: The RepoGlance Pinned repos widget: three made-up repositories, each with the time of its data and its open issue and pull request counts
The RepoGlance Pinned repos widget: three made-up repositories, each with the time of its data and its open issue and pull request counts

layout.heading: In the app
layout.body: Browse every repository you share with RepoGlance, filter by account or organization, search, sort by latest push, and pin from the row. Open one to read its open issues and pull requests; tap to continue in the GitHub app.

$media.alt: Rows of the RepoGlance catalog: made-up repositories with their visibility and last push, pinned ones first
Rows of the RepoGlance catalog: made-up repositories with their visibility and last push, pinned ones first

layout.heading: In Quick Settings
layout.body: The RepoGlance tile shows your latest push with its age. Pinned repositories refresh about every 30 minutes on a network connection; when GitHub can't be reached, you see the last good value or no data, never a made-up zero.

$media.alt: The Quick Settings row with the RepoGlance tile showing the latest push to a made-up repository, beside the Internet tile
The Quick Settings row with the RepoGlance tile showing the latest push to a made-up repository, beside the Internet tile

layout.heading: When you sign in
layout.body: Sign in on GitHub's own page. RepoGlance shows a short code; Copy code & open GitHub takes you to GitHub to enter it and authorize. RepoGlance never sees your password. No account yet? Tap Explore with sample data instead.

layout.heading: What stays true all day
layout.intro: The rules RepoGlance keeps, whatever the numbers do.

items.text: It only reads. RepoGlance never comments, closes, merges or changes anything on GitHub.
It has no server. Your phone talks to GitHub directly.
You sign in on GitHub's own page with a short code; RepoGlance never sees your password. The token is encrypted with Android Keystore.
It carries no ads, analytics or trackers. Disconnect GitHub in Settings and the session and cached data are deleted from the phone.
It never fakes a number: unknown is not zero, stale data wears its age, a rate limit is shown.
Not yet: a CI column. This build does not fetch CI state.

layout.heading: Help test RepoGlance
layout.body: RepoGlance 0.4.0-beta.1 is in closed testing on Google Play. It is made for Pixel phones and foldables, with Material You dynamic color and light and dark themes. Join the testers group to get the build.

data.title: Join the closed test
data.description: How to get the RepoGlance closed test onto your Pixel: join the testers group, accept the test on Google Play, install.

layout.heading: Get the test build on your Pixel.
layout.lead: RepoGlance 0.4.0-beta.1 is a closed test on Google Play for Pixel phones and foldables on Android 12 or newer. Bring the Google account you use on Google Play; the rest takes a few minutes.

$media.alt: The RepoGlance sign-in screen: a short code to enter on GitHub, how long it lasts, and the Copy code & open GitHub button; the code shown is made up
The RepoGlance sign-in screen: a short code to enter on GitHub, how long it lasts, and the Copy code & open GitHub button; the code shown is made up

layout.heading: Three steps, in order
layout.intro: Group first, Play second, install third.

steps.text: Join the RepoGlance testers Google Group with the Google account you use on Google Play. Anyone on the web can join.
Accept the test on Google Play. The opt-in link is not published yet; it will appear here as soon as Google Play shows it.
Install RepoGlance from Google Play. First screen: Sign in with GitHub, or Explore with sample data.

layout.note: Joining the group installs nothing. Leaving the group leaves the test.

items.text: GitHub device-flow sign-in; the catalog of repositories your installation shares; pin from the row.
Per-repository open issues and pull requests; a tap opens the GitHub app.
Repository widget, Pinned repos widget, Quick Settings tile; sample mode for all three.
Settings: theme (Light, Dark, System default), Manage GitHub access, Disconnect GitHub.
Not yet: a CI column, the latest release, account-wide navigation.

layout.heading: Feedback
layout.body: Say what happened in a GitHub issue: which phone, which Android version, and whether you were signed in or in sample mode.

layout.heading: Privacy
layout.body: Nothing leaves your phone except requests to GitHub. The privacy policy explains what is stored on the phone and how to remove it.
